parallel.requirements: The parallel root recognized the required Rust 2021 project, root test5.rs, standard-library-only implementation, byte-for-byte output, and C++-compatible argument parsing including stoi-like prefixes and default behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The root kept implementation ownership while delegating a structure/layout check and a semantic edge-case check; the semantic child further spawned a nested checker.
parallel.implementation: The root implemented Cargo.toml, test5.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, src/hopscotch_map.rs, and src/program.rs, then patched src/program.rs so direct rustc compilation resolved the module path correctly.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The root integrated its own files into /output, kept the required entry point at /output/test5.rs, built /output/test5 and target/release/test5, and delivered the project.
parallel.verification: The root ran Cargo tests, Cargo release build, direct rustc build, and reference-output comparisons for samples and malformed or edge CLI inputs.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No required task behavior remained unfinished at closure; an auxiliary semantic child path was interrupted after the root had enough evidence and the official evaluator passed.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same Rust 2021, no-crates, root test5.rs, CLI parity, exact output, Cargo project, and black-box behavior requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial agent owned all probing, implementation, module layout, compile repair, and verification locally without delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial agent implemented Cargo.toml, test5.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, src/hopscotch_map.rs, and src/app.rs, then patched test5.rs after the first compile exposed a module-root mismatch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial solution placed the required files in /output, compiled the root entry directly and through Cargo, and delivered a complete project.
serial.verification: The serial run checked sample outputs, direct rustc, cargo build --release, cargo test, negative counts, nonmatching first argument, and stoi-style numeric prefixes against the C++ executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No required task behavior remained unfinished at closure, and the official evaluator passed all 39 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run treated exact CLI behavior, stoi-like parsing, no external crates, Cargo layout, root test5.rs, and byte-for-byte output as required.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same requirements and used local probing to confirm examples and edge CLI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement difference affected the outcome; both runs solved the required C++ behavior and project-structure obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The root assigned auxiliary structure and semantic checking to children but kept the implementation, patching, build, and final delivery work itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single serial agent owned investigation, implementation, compile repair, verification, and delivery end to end.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used delegation for checks, while serial stayed local; ownership of the deliverable remained clear in both attempts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The structure child returned an applicable root-entry layout recommendation, and the root later observed child status that included the nested semantic findings.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no inter-agent context boundary; it preserved task knowledge within one agent while patching and testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had handoffs and one incomplete child lifecycle, but the handoffs did not cause incompatible interfaces or unmet requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel root wrote the project files, including a HashMap-backed hopscotch wrapper and stoi-like parser, then fixed a crate-path issue in src/program.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote a similar project and fixed its module-root mismatch by changing the root test5.rs module declarations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file/module names differed slightly, but both implementation paths converged on equivalent behavior and successful builds.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The root waited for child work, got a timed wait, inspected live/completed agents with list_agents, and then finalized after its own build and behavior checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child-result lifecycle and closed only after local compile and runtime checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra child-result management overhead, but no child result became necessary for final correctness or official success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The root wrote and patched the final /output files itself; child work did not overwrite the required deliverable or create a conflicting final tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote the final /output files itself, then patched test5.rs to align direct rustc and Cargo builds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material shared-state collision separated the outcomes; both final artifacts validated successfully.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel root ran cargo test, cargo build --release, direct rustc, output comparisons, and then the official evaluator completed 39/39.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run ran direct rustc, cargo build --release, output checks, cargo test, edge-case comparisons, and then the official evaluator completed 39/39.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verification paths were evaluator-aligned and successful, with serial doing one visible compile-fix cycle and parallel doing auxiliary child checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used more elapsed time and token budget because of child activity, but closed after completed builds, tests, and reference comparisons.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used a smaller single-agent budget and closed after its local verification completed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel overhead did not displace required work; both attempts closed with complete artifacts and passed official evaluation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The completed official evaluation in each mode passed all 39 testcases, so the outcome relation is both_pass. The parallel run used child agents for layout and semantic checking while the root retained implementation and verification control; the serial run did all probing, implementation, compile repair, and verification locally. The strategies differed in coordination overhead, but both produced equivalent accepted Rust projects.
parallel_contributors: The root implemented and patched the final project itself, then built with both Cargo and rustc.
The root compared runtime behavior with the C++ executable for examples and edge cases before finalizing.
serial_contributors: The serial agent corrected its module-root compile error and rebuilt successfully.
The serial agent verified sample outputs and additional stoi-style cases before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used src/program.rs and a library named test5lib, while serial used src/app.rs and a library named test5_migration.
Serial initially failed compilation because of a module-root mismatch and fixed test5.rs; parallel fixed a related module path before its successful build.
